questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function defined by $f(x) = \|x+2\| - 2|x|$. If $m$ is the number of points of local minima and $n$ is the number of points of local maxima of $f$, then $m + n$ is
questions.solution_text: We have $f(x) = |x+2| - 2|x|$. Critical points arise at $x = 0$ and $x = -2$. We also check $x = -2/3$ by solving where the slope changes. Analysing the function piecewise: For $x < -2$: $f(x) = -(x+2) - 2(-x) = -x-2+2x = x-2$, slope = 1. For $-2 \le x < 0$: $f(x) = (x+2) - 2(-x) = x+2+2x = 3x+2$, slope = 3. For $x \ge 0$: $f(x) = (x+2) - 2x = -x+2$, slope = -1. From the graph analysis, there is 1 local maximum (at $x=0$, value $f(0)=2$) and 2 local minima (at $x=-2$, value $f(-2)=-2+4=2$ ... re-examining: at $x=-2$, slope changes from 1 to 3, both positive, so not extremum. At $x=0$, slope changes from 3 to -1, so local maximum. The function $f(x)=||x+2|-2|x||$ — reconsidering: the critical points are $x=0,-2,-2/3$. Number of maxima $n=1$, number of minima $m=2$, so $m+n=3$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Each of the angles $\beta$ and $\gamma$ that a given line makes with the positive $y$-axis and $z$-axis, respectively, is half of the angle that this line makes with the positive $x$-axis. Then the sum of all possible values of the angle $\beta$ is
questions.solution_text: Let $\alpha$ be the angle with positive $x$-axis. Then $\beta = \alpha/2$ and $\gamma = \alpha/2$. Using $\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1$: $\cos^2\alpha + 2\cos^2(\alpha/2) = 1$. Using $\cos^2(\alpha/2) = (1+\cos\alpha)/2$: $\cos^2\alpha + (1+\cos\alpha) = 1$, so $\cos^2\alpha + \cos\alpha = 0$, giving $\cos\alpha(\cos\alpha+1)=0$, so $\cos\alpha = 0$ or $\cos\alpha = -1$, i.e., $\alpha = \pi/2$ or $\alpha = \pi$. Now $\beta = \alpha/2$: when $\alpha = \pi/2$, $\beta = \pi/4$; when $\alpha = \pi$, $\beta = \pi/2$. Sum $= \pi/4 + \pi/2 = 3\pi/4$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: If the four distinct points $(4, 6)$, $(-1, 5)$, $(0, 0)$ and $(k, 3k)$ lie on a circle of radius $r$, then $10k + r^2$ is equal to
questions.solution_text: Since $(4,6)$, $(-1,5)$, $(0,0)$ lie on the circle. The angle subtended by $(4,6)$ and $(0,0)$ at $(-1,5)$: slope of line joining $(4,6)$ and $(-1,5)$ is $m_1 = 1/5$; slope joining $(4,6)$ and $(0,0)$ is $3/2$. Actually, since $(4,6)$, $(-1,5)$, $(0,0)$ form a right angle (check: $m_1 \cdot m_2 = -1$?). Slope of $(4,6)$ to $(0,0)$ is $6/4=3/2$; slope of $(-1,5)$ to $(0,0)$ is $-5$; product $= -15/2 \ne -1$. Use the circle equation through $(0,0)$: $x^2+y^2+Dx+Ey=0$. Substituting $(-1,5)$: $1+25-D+5E=0 \Rightarrow D-5E=26$. Substituting $(4,6)$: $16+36+4D+6E=0 \Rightarrow 4D+6E=-52 \Rightarrow 2D+3E=-26$. From first: $D=26+5E$. Substituting: $2(26+5E)+3E=-26 \Rightarrow 52+13E=-26 \Rightarrow E=-6, D=-4$. Circle: $x^2+y^2-4x-6y=0$. $(k,3k)$ lies on it: $k^2+9k^2-4k-18k=0 \Rightarrow 10k^2-22k=0 \Rightarrow k(10k-22)=0 \Rightarrow k=0$ (rejected, coincides with origin) or $k=11/5$. Radius $r=\sqrt{4+9}=\sqrt{13}$, so $r^2=13$. $10k+r^2 = 10(11/5)+13 = 22+13=35$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Consider the lines $x(3\lambda+1) + y(7\lambda+2) = 17\lambda+5$, $\lambda$ being a parameter, all passing through a point $P$. One of these lines (say $L$) is farthest from the origin. If the distance of $L$ from the point $(3, 6)$ is $d$, then the value of $d^2$ is
questions.solution_text: Rewrite: $x(3\lambda+1)+y(7\lambda+2)=17\lambda+5 \Rightarrow (x+2y-5)+\lambda(3x+7y-17)=0$. This is the family passing through the intersection of $x+2y-5=0$ and $3x+7y-17=0$. Solving: from first, $x=5-2y$; substituting: $3(5-2y)+7y=17 \Rightarrow 15+y=17 \Rightarrow y=2, x=1$. So $P=(1,2)$. The line $L$ farthest from origin passes through $P=(1,2)$ and is perpendicular to $OP$. Slope of $OP = 2/1=2$, so slope of $L = -1/2$. Line $L$: $y-2 = -\frac{1}{2}(x-1) \Rightarrow x+2y-5=0$. Distance from $(3,6)$: $d = |3+12-5|/\sqrt{5} = 10/\sqrt{5} = 2\sqrt{5}$. $d^2=20$.

questions.question_text: Let the equation $x(x+2)(12-k) = 2$ have equal roots. Then the distance of the point $\left(k, \dfrac{k}{2}\right)$ from the line $3x+4y+5=0$ is
questions.solution_text:
$(x^2+2x)(12-k)=2$. Let $\lambda=12-k$, so $\lambda x^2+2\lambda x-2=0$ (assuming $\lambda
e 0$, i.e., $k
e 12$). For equal roots: discriminant $=0$. $D=(2\lambda)^2+4\cdot\lambda\cdot 2=4\lambda^2+8\lambda=0 \Rightarrow 4\lambda(\lambda+2)=0 \Rightarrow \lambda=0$ or $\lambda=-2$. Since $k
e 12$, $\lambda=-2 \Rightarrow 12-k=-2 \Rightarrow k=14$. Point: $(14, 7)$. Distance from $3x+4y+5=0$: $d=|3(14)+4(7)+5|/\sqrt{9+16}=|42+28+5|/5=75/5=15$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Line $L_1$ of slope 2 and line $L_2$ of slope $\dfrac{1}{2}$ intersect at the origin $O$. In the first quadrant, $P_1, P_2, \ldots, P_{12}$ are 12 points on line $L_1$ and $Q_1, Q_2, \ldots, Q_9$ are 9 points on line $L_2$. Then the total number of triangles, that can be formed having vertices at three of the 22 points $O, P_1, P_2, \ldots, P_{12}, Q_1, Q_2, \ldots, Q_9$, is
questions.solution_text: Total 22 points: $O$, 12 on $L_1$, 9 on $L_2$. Points on same line are collinear. Total triangles = Total $\binom{22}{3}$ minus collinear combinations. Collinear sets: 13 points on $L_1$ (O + 12), 10 on $L_2$ (O + 9). Triangles = $\binom{22}{3} - \binom{13}{3} - \binom{10}{3}$. But we can directly count: choose 1 from $L_2$ group and 2 from $L_1$ group; or 2 from $L_2$ and 1 from $L_1$; or 1 from each line and $O$; or 2 from $L_1$ and $O$ — but $O,P_i,P_j$ are collinear. More carefully: valid triangles need points not all on same line. $= {}^9C_1 \cdot {}^{12}C_2 + {}^9C_2 \cdot {}^{12}C_1 + {}^1C_1 \cdot {}^9C_1 \cdot {}^{12}C_1 = 9\cdot66 + 36\cdot12 + 9\cdot12 = 594+432+108=1134$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: The integral $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi} \dfrac{8x\,dx}{4\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x}$ is equal to
questions.solution_text: Let $I = \int_0^\pi \frac{8x\,dx}{4\cos^2x+\sin^2x}$. Using $\int_0^\pi f(x)dx = \int_0^\pi f(\pi-x)dx$: $I=\int_0^\pi \frac{8(\pi-x)}{4\cos^2x+\sin^2x}dx$. Adding: $2I = 8\pi\int_0^\pi \frac{dx}{4\cos^2x+\sin^2x}$. Using symmetry about $\pi/2$: $2I=16\pi\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{dx}{4\cos^2x+\sin^2x}$. Divide numerator and denominator by $\cos^2x$: $= 16\pi\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\sec^2x\,dx}{4+\tan^2x}$. Let $t=\tan x$: $=16\pi\int_0^\infty \frac{dt}{4+t^2} = 16\pi \cdot \frac{1}{2}[\tan^{-1}(t/2)]_0^\infty = 16\pi \cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{\pi}{2}=4\pi^2$. So $I=2\pi^2$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: The area of the region $\{(x,y): |x-y| \le y \le 4\sqrt{x}\}$ is
questions.solution_text: Condition: $|x-y|\le y$ means $-y\le x-y\le y$, i.e., $0\le x\le 2y$ i.e., $y\ge x/2$. And $y\le 4\sqrt{x}$. The boundary $y=|x-y|$ gives $y=x/2$ (for $x\ge 0$) and $y=0$ implies $x=0$. Intersection of $y=x/2$ and $y=4\sqrt{x}$: $x/2=4\sqrt{x} \Rightarrow \sqrt{x}=8 \Rightarrow x=64, y=32$. Area $= \int_0^{64}\left(4\sqrt{x}-\frac{x}{2}\right)dx = \left[\frac{4x^{3/2}}{3/2}-\frac{x^2}{4}\right]_0^{64} = \frac{8}{3}\cdot 512 - \frac{64^2}{4} = \frac{4096}{3}-1024 = \frac{4096-3072}{3}=\frac{1024}{3}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: If the domain of the function $f(x) = \log_7(1 - \log_4(x^2 - 9x + 18))$ is $(\alpha, \beta) \cup (\gamma, \delta)$, then $\alpha + \beta + \gamma + \delta$ is equal to
questions.solution_text: Need: (1) $x^2-9x+18>0$ and (2) $1-\log_4(x^2-9x+18)>0$. From (1): $(x-3)(x-6)>0 \Rightarrow x\in(-\infty,3)\cup(6,\infty)$. From (2): $\log_4(x^2-9x+18)<1 \Rightarrow x^2-9x+18<4 \Rightarrow x^2-9x+14<0 \Rightarrow (x-2)(x-7)<0 \Rightarrow x\in(2,7)$. Intersection of (1) and (2): $(2,3)\cup(6,7)=( \alpha,\beta)\cup(\gamma,\delta)$. So $\alpha=2,\beta=3,\gamma=6,\delta=7$, and $\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta=18$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Let $y = y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 3(\tan^2 x)\,y + 3y = \sec^2 x$, $y(0) = \dfrac{1}{3} + e^3$. Then $y\!\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution_text: Equation: $\frac{dy}{dx}+3(\tan^2x+1)y=\sec^2x \Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}+3\sec^2x\cdot y=\sec^2x$. IF $= e^{\int 3\sec^2x\,dx}=e^{3\tan x}$. Solution: $e^{3\tan x}y=\int e^{3\tan x}\sec^2x\,dx$. Let $u=3\tan x$, $du=3\sec^2x\,dx$: $=\frac{1}{3}\int e^u\,du=\frac{e^{3\tan x}}{3}+C$. So $y=\frac{1}{3}+Ce^{-3\tan x}$. At $x=0$: $y(0)=\frac{1}{3}+C=\frac{1}{3}+e^3 \Rightarrow C=e^3$. $y=\frac{1}{3}+e^3 e^{-3\tan x}$. At $x=\pi/4$: $\tan(\pi/4)=1$, $y=\frac{1}{3}+e^3\cdot e^{-3}=\frac{1}{3}+1=\frac{4}{3}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: If $z_1, z_2, z_3 \in \mathbb{C}$ are the vertices of an equilateral triangle, whose centroid is $z_0$, then $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{3}(z_k - z_0)^2$ is equal to
questions.solution_text: $z_0=(z_1+z_2+z_3)/3$, so $z_1+z_2+z_3=3z_0$. $\sum(z_k-z_0)^2 = \sum z_k^2 - 2z_0\sum z_k + 3z_0^2 = \sum z_k^2 - 2z_0\cdot3z_0+3z_0^2 = \sum z_k^2 - 3z_0^2$. Now $(z_1+z_2+z_3)^2=\sum z_k^2+2\sum_{i<j}z_iz_j=9z_0^2$. For equilateral triangle: $z_1^2+z_2^2+z_3^2=z_1z_2+z_2z_3+z_3z_1$ (known property). Also $\sum z_iz_j = \frac{9z_0^2-\sum z_k^2}{2}$. Using property: $\sum z_k^2=\sum_{i<j}z_iz_j$. So $9z_0^2 = \sum z_k^2 + 2\sum z_k^2 = 3\sum z_k^2 \Rightarrow \sum z_k^2=3z_0^2$. Therefore $\sum(z_k-z_0)^2=3z_0^2-3z_0^2=0$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.topic: Ellipse and Circle - Maximum Area of Triangle
questions.question_text: Let $C$ be the circle of minimum area enclosing the ellipse $E: \dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$ with eccentricity $\dfrac{1}{2}$ and foci $(\pm 2, 0)$. Let $PQR$ be a variable triangle, whose vertex $P$ is on the circle $C$ and the side $QR$ of length 29 is parallel to the major axis of $E$ and contains the point of intersection of $E$ with the negative $y$-axis. Then the maximum area of the triangle $PQR$ is
questions.solution_text: Eccentricity $e=1/2$, foci $(\pm 2,0)$: $ae=2 \Rightarrow a\cdot(1/2)=2 \Rightarrow a=4$. $b^2=a^2(1-e^2)=16\cdot 3/4=12 \Rightarrow b=2\sqrt{3}$. Circle of minimum area enclosing ellipse has radius $a=4$ (the semi-major axis). Let $P=(4\cos\theta, 4\sin\theta)$ on circle. Side $QR$ passes through $(0,-b)=(0,-2\sqrt{3})$ and is parallel to $x$-axis: $y=-2\sqrt{3}$. Length $QR=2a=8$ (chord of ellipse at $y=-b$ is at vertex, giving length... actually the side $QR$ is at $y=-2\sqrt{3}$ with length 29 — wait, re-reading: length 29 seems large, the answer uses area of $\triangle PQR = \frac{1}{2}\cdot QR \cdot h$ where $h$ is height from $P$ to $QR$. Max height = max $(y_P - (-2\sqrt{3})) = 4+2\sqrt{3}$ (when $P$ is at top of circle). Max area $= \frac{1}{2}\cdot 2a\cdot(a+b)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 8\cdot(4+2\sqrt{3})=4(4+2\sqrt{3})=8(2+\sqrt{3})$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: The shortest distance between the curves $y^2 = 8x$ and $x^2 + y^2 + 12y + 35 = 0$ is
questions.solution_text: Circle: $x^2+(y+6)^2=1$, centre $C(0,-6)$, radius $r=1$. Parabola: $y^2=8x$, so $a=2$. Normal to parabola at point $(2t^2, 4t)$ passes through $C(0,-6)$: normal equation $y=-tx+4t+2t^3$. Passing through $(0,-6)$: $-6=4t+2t^3 \Rightarrow 2t^3+4t+6=0 \Rightarrow t^3+2t+3=0 \Rightarrow (t+1)(t^2-t+3)=0 \Rightarrow t=-1$. Point $P=(2,-4)$. $PC=\sqrt{(2-0)^2+(-4+6)^2}=\sqrt{4+4}=2\sqrt{2}$. Shortest distance $=PC-r=2\sqrt{2}-1$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.topic: Distance between Skew Lines / Point-Line Distance
questions.question_text: The distance of the point $(7, 10, 11)$ from the line $\dfrac{x-4}{1} = \dfrac{y-4}{0} = \dfrac{z-2}{3}$ along the line $\dfrac{x-9}{2} = \dfrac{y-13}{3} = \dfrac{z-17}{6}$ is
questions.solution_text: Line through $P(7,10,11)$ along direction $(2,3,6)$: parametrically $(7+2\lambda, 10+3\lambda, 11+6\lambda)$. This must lie on the first line $\frac{x-4}{1}=\frac{y-4}{0}=\frac{z-2}{3}$. Since $y-4=0$: $10+3\lambda=4 \Rightarrow \lambda=-2$. Check: $x=7-4=3$, $z=11-12=-1$. Verify on first line: $\frac{3-4}{1}=-1$, $\frac{-1-2}{3}=-1$. Yes! So $Q=(3,4,-1)$. $PQ=\sqrt{(7-3)^2+(10-4)^2+(11+1)^2}=\sqrt{16+36+144}=\sqrt{196}=14$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: The sum $1 + \dfrac{1+3}{2!} + \dfrac{1+3+5}{3!} + \dfrac{1+3+5+7}{4!} + \cdots$ up to $\infty$ terms, is equal to
questions.solution_text: The $r$-th term has numerator $1+3+5+\cdots+(2r-1)=r^2$, so $S=\sum_{r=1}^\infty \frac{r^2}{r!} = \sum_{r=1}^\infty \frac{r(r-1)+r}{r!}=\sum_{r=2}^\infty\frac{1}{(r-2)!}+\sum_{r=1}^\infty\frac{1}{(r-1)!}=e+e=2e$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Let $I$ be the identity matrix of order $3\times3$ and for the matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} \lambda & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$, $|A|=-1$. Let $B$ be the inverse of the matrix $\text{adj}(A\cdot\text{adj}(A^2))$. Then $|(\lambda B+I)|$ is equal to ______
questions.solution_text: Given $|A|=-1$. From $|A|=\lambda(10+6)-2(8-42)+3(-4-35)=-1$: $16\lambda+68-117=-1 \Rightarrow 16\lambda=48 \Rightarrow \lambda=3$. Now find $B^{-1}=\text{adj}(A\cdot\text{adj}(A^2))$. Let $C=A\cdot\text{adj}(A^2)$. $\text{adj}(A^2)=|A^2|\cdot(A^2)^{-1}=1\cdot(A^2)^{-1}=(A^{-1})^2$ (since $|A|^2=1$). So $C=A(A^{-1})^2=A^{-1}=\text{adj}(A)/|A|=-\text{adj}(A)$. $B=C^{-1}=(A^{-1})^{-1}=A$... actually $B^{-1}=\text{adj}(C)$ means $B=(\text{adj}(C))^{-1}$. Since $\text{adj}(C)=|C|C^{-1}$ and $C=A^{-1}$: $|C|=|A^{-1}|=-1$, $C^{-1}=A$. So $\text{adj}(C)=-A$, giving $B=(-A)^{-1}=-A^{-1}=-\text{adj}(A)$ (since $|A|=-1$, $A^{-1}=\text{adj}(A)/(-1)=-\text{adj}(A)$, so $B=\text{adj}(A)$). $\lambda B+I=3\text{adj}(A)+I=P$. $AP=3A\text{adj}(A)+A=3|A|I+A=−3I+A$. $|A||P|=|A-3I|$. $A-3I=\begin{pmatrix}0&2&3\\4&2&6\\7&-1&-1\end{pmatrix}$. $|A-3I|=0(−2+6)−2(−4−42)+3(−4−14)=0+92−54=38$. $|A||P|=38 \Rightarrow (-1)|P|=38 \Rightarrow |P|=-38$. $|(\lambda B+I)|=38$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: If $\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{\tan x}{x}\right)^{1/x^2} = p$, then $96\log_e p$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution_text: $\ln p = \lim_{x\to0}\frac{1}{x^2}\ln\frac{\tan x}{x}$. Use expansion: $\tan x = x+x^3/3+2x^5/15+\cdots$, so $\frac{\tan x}{x}=1+x^2/3+\cdots$. $\ln\frac{\tan x}{x}=\ln(1+x^2/3+\cdots)\approx x^2/3+O(x^4)$. $\ln p=\lim_{x\to0}\frac{x^2/3}{x^2}=1/3$. $96\ln p=96\times\frac{1}{3}=32$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Let $\vec{a} = \hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}=3\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$, $\vec{c}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{d}$ be a vector such that $\vec{b}\times\vec{d}=\vec{c}\times\vec{d}$ and $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{d}=4$. Then $|\vec{a}\times\vec{d}|^2$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution_text: $\vec{b}\times\vec{d}=\vec{c}\times\vec{d} \Rightarrow (\vec{b}-\vec{c})\times\vec{d}=\vec{0} \Rightarrow \vec{d}\parallel(\vec{b}-\vec{c})$. $\vec{b}-\vec{c}=(3-2)\hat{i}+(-3+1)\hat{j}+(3-2)\hat{k}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k}$. So $\vec{d}=\lambda(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k})$. $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{d}=\lambda(1\cdot1+2\cdot(-2)+1\cdot1)=\lambda(1-4+1)=-2\lambda=4 \Rightarrow \lambda=-2$. $\vec{d}=-2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$. $|\vec{d}|^2=4+16+4=24$, $|\vec{a}|^2=1+4+1=6$. $|\vec{a}\times\vec{d}|^2=|\vec{a}|^2|\vec{d}|^2-(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{d})^2=6\cdot24-16=144-16=128$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: If the equation of the hyperbola with foci $(4, 2)$ and $(8, 2)$ is $3x^2 - y^2 - \alpha x + \beta y + \gamma = 0$, then $\alpha + \beta + \gamma$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution_text: Foci $(4,2)$ and $(8,2)$: centre $C=(6,2)$, $c=2$. The hyperbola has form $\frac{(x-6)^2}{a^2}-\frac{(y-2)^2}{b^2}=1$. Since comparing with $3x^2-y^2-\alpha x+\beta y+\gamma=0$, coefficients of $x^2$ and $y^2$ are 3 and -1, ratio is 3:1. So $b^2/a^2=3$. With $c^2=a^2+b^2=4$: $a^2+3a^2=4 \Rightarrow a^2=1, b^2=3$. Hyperbola: $(x-6)^2-\frac{(y-2)^2}{3}=1 \Rightarrow 3(x-6)^2-(y-2)^2=3$. Expanding: $3(x^2-12x+36)-(y^2-4y+4)=3$. $3x^2-36x+108-y^2+4y-4=3$. $3x^2-y^2-36x+4y+101=0$. So $\alpha=36, \beta=4$ (noting sign: $-\alpha x$ means $\alpha=36$, $+\beta y$ means $\beta=4$... wait: equation is $3x^2-y^2-\alpha x+\beta y+\gamma=0$ vs $3x^2-y^2-36x+4y+101=0$). $\alpha=36, \beta=4, \gamma=101$. $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=141$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A magnetic dipole experiences a torque of $80\sqrt{3}$ N·m when placed in a uniform magnetic field in such a way that the dipole moment makes an angle of $60°$ with the magnetic field. The potential energy of the dipole is
questions.solution_text: $\tau = MB\sin60° = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}MB = 80\sqrt{3} \Rightarrow MB=160$. Potential energy $U=-MB\cos60°=-160\times\frac{1}{2}=-80$ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Beats and Resonance in Organ Pipes
questions.question_text: In the resonance experiment, two air columns (closed at one end) of 100 cm and 120 cm long, give 15 beats per second when each one is sounding in the respective fundamental modes. The velocity of sound in the air column is
questions.solution_text: Fundamental frequency of closed pipe: $f=v/(4\ell)$. $f_1=v/4, f_2=v/4.8$ (in SI, $\ell_1=1$ m, $\ell_2=1.2$ m). Beats $=f_1-f_2=v/4\left(1-\frac{1}{1.2}\right)=\frac{v}{4}\cdot\frac{0.2}{1.2}=\frac{v}{24}=15 \Rightarrow v=360$ m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Work Done by Gravity - Connected Vessels
questions.question_text: Two cylindrical vessels of equal cross-sectional area of $2\text{ m}^2$ contain water up to heights 10 m and 6 m, respectively. If the vessels are connected at their bottom, then the work done by the force of gravity is (Density of water is $10^3$ kg/m$^3$ and $g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution_text: After connecting, final height = $(10+6)/2=8$ m in each. Initial PE: $U_i = \rho A g[10\cdot5 + 6\cdot3]=\rho Ag(50+18)=68\rho Ag$. Final PE: $U_f=\rho Ag[8\cdot4+8\cdot4]=64\rho Ag$. Work done by gravity $=U_i-U_f=4\rho Ag=4\times1000\times2\times10=8\times10^4$ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An ideal gas exists in a state with pressure $P_0$, volume $V_0$. It is isothermally expanded to 4 times of its initial volume ($V_0$), then isobarically compressed to its original volume. Finally the system is heated isochorically to bring it to its initial state. The amount of heat exchanged in this process is
questions.solution_text: Process 1→2 (isothermal): $W_1=P_0V_0\ln4=2P_0V_0\ln2$. Final pressure at 2: $P_0V_0=P_2(4V_0) \Rightarrow P_2=P_0/4$. Process 2→3 (isobaric, $P=P_0/4$, volume $4V_0\to V_0$): $W_2=\frac{P_0}{4}(V_0-4V_0)=-\frac{3P_0V_0}{4}$. Process 3→1 (isochoric): $W_3=0$. Total work $W=W_1+W_2=P_0V_0(2\ln2-3/4)=P_0V_0(2\ln2-0.75)$. For cyclic process, $\Delta U=0$, so $Q=W=P_0V_0(2\ln2-0.75)$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as **Assertion A** and the other is labelled as **Reason R**.

**Assertion A:** The Bohr model is applicable to hydrogen and hydrogen-like atoms only.

**Reason R:** The formulation of Bohr model does not include repulsive force between electrons.

In the light of the above statements, choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

questions.solution_text: Bohr model applies only to single-electron systems (H and H-like atoms). This is because the model does not account for electron-electron repulsion. Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Using a battery, a 100 pF capacitor is charged to 60 V and then the battery is removed. After that, a second uncharged capacitor is connected to the first capacitor in parallel. If the final voltage across the second capacitor is 20 V, its capacitance is (in pF)
questions.solution_text: Initial charge $Q=C_0V_0=100\times60=6000$ pC. After connecting $C$ in parallel, common voltage $V_f=Q/(C_0+C)=20$ V. $C_0+C=6000/20=300$ pF. $C=300-100=200$ pF.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A monochromatic light of frequency $5\times10^{14}$ Hz travelling through air, is incident on a medium of refractive index '2'. Wavelength of the refracted light will be
questions.solution_text: $\lambda_{medium}=\frac{\lambda_{vacuum}}{\mu}=\frac{v}{f\mu}=\frac{3\times10^8}{5\times10^{14}\times2}=\frac{3\times10^8}{10^{15}}=3\times10^{-7}$ m $=300$ nm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Consider two blocks A and B of masses $m_1=10$ kg and $m_2=5$ kg that are placed on a frictionless table. The block A moves with a constant speed $v=3$ m/s towards the block B kept at rest. A spring with spring constant $k=3000$ N/m is attached with the block B as shown in the figure. After the collision, suppose that the blocks A and B, along with the spring in constant compression state, move together. Then the compression in the spring is (Neglect the mass of the spring)
questions.solution_text: By conservation of momentum: $m_1v=(m_1+m_2)v_{cm}$. $v_{cm}=10\times3/15=2$ m/s. By energy conservation: $\frac{1}{2}kx^2=\frac{1}{2}m_1v^2-\frac{1}{2}(m_1+m_2)v_{cm}^2=\frac{1}{2}(10)(9)-\frac{1}{2}(15)(4)=45-30=15$ J. $x^2=30/3000=1/100 \Rightarrow x=0.1$ m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A particle is projected with velocity $u$ so that its horizontal range is three times the maximum height attained by it. The horizontal range of the projectile is given as $\dfrac{nu^2}{25g}$, where the value of $n$ is (Given '$g$' is the acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution_text: Range $R=\frac{u^2\sin2\theta}{g}$, $H_{max}=\frac{u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$. Given $R=3H_{max}$: $\frac{u^2\sin2\theta}{g}=\frac{3u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$. $2\sin\theta\cos\theta\cdot2=3\sin^2\theta \Rightarrow 4\cos\theta=3\sin\theta \Rightarrow \tan\theta=4/3$. So $\sin\theta=4/5, \cos\theta=3/5$. $R=\frac{u^2\cdot2\cdot(3/5)\cdot(4/5)}{g}=\frac{24u^2}{25g}$. So $n=24$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A solid steel ball of diameter 3.6 mm acquired terminal velocity $2.45\times10^{-2}$ m/s while falling under gravity through an oil of density 925 kg m$^{-3}$. Take density of steel as 7825 kg m$^{-3}$ and $g$ as 9.8 m/s$^2$. The viscosity of the oil in SI unit is
questions.solution_text: $v_T=\frac{2r^2(\rho-\rho_f)g}{9\eta}$. $r=1.8\times10^{-3}$ m. $\eta=\frac{2(1.8\times10^{-3})^2(7825-925)\times9.8}{9\times2.45\times10^{-2}}=\frac{2\times3.24\times10^{-6}\times6900\times9.8}{9\times0.0245}=\frac{2\times3.24\times6900\times9.8\times10^{-6}}{0.2205}\approx1.99$ Pa·s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The truth table corresponding to the circuit given below (an OR gate followed by a NOT gate output, with the original A as additional AND input) is: The circuit shows: A and B as inputs to an OR gate, output $(A+B)$; then AND gate with inputs A and $(A+B)$, giving $C=A\cdot(A+B)$.
questions.solution_text: From circuit: $C=A\cdot(A+B)$. Truth table: $(0,0)$: $C=0\cdot0=0$; $(0,1)$: $C=0\cdot1=0$; $(1,0)$: $C=1\cdot1=1$; $(1,1)$: $C=1\cdot1=1$. This matches option (2).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A particle moves along the $x$-axis and has its displacement $x$ varying with time $t$ according to the equation $x = c_0(t^2 - 2) + c(t-2)^2$ where $c_0$ and $c$ are constants of appropriate dimensions. Then, which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: the acceleration of the particle is $2c_0$
the acceleration of the particle is $2c$
the initial velocity of the particle is $4c$
the acceleration of the particle is $2(c+c_0)$

questions.solution_text: $x=c_0(t^2-2)+c(t-2)^2$. $v=\frac{dx}{dt}=2c_0t+2c(t-2)$. $a=\frac{dv}{dt}=2c_0+2c=2(c_0+c)$. At $t=0$: $v=0-4c=-4c$ (initial velocity is $-4c$, not $4c$). Acceleration is constant $=2(c+c_0)$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An electric bulb rated as 100 W-220 V is connected to an ac source of rms voltage 220 V. The peak value of current through the bulb is
questions.solution_text: $i_{rms}=P/V_{rms}=100/220$ A. $i_0=\sqrt{2}\cdot i_{rms}=\sqrt{2}\times100/220=\sqrt{2}/2.2\approx0.64$ A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
Match the **LIST-I** with **LIST-II**:

| | LIST-I | | LIST-II |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. | Boltzmann constant | I. | $ML^2T^{-1}$ |
| B. | Coefficient of viscosity | II. | $MLT^{-3}K^{-1}$ |
| C. | Planck's constant | III. | $ML^2T^{-2}K^{-1}$ |
| D. | Thermal conductivity | IV. | $ML^{-1}T^{-1}$ |

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: A. Boltzmann constant $[k]=PV/T=ML^2T^{-2}K^{-1}$ → III. B. Coefficient of viscosity $[\eta]=ML^{-1}T^{-1}$ → IV. C. Planck's constant $[h]=E/f=ML^2T^{-2}/T^{-1}=ML^2T^{-1}$ → I. D. Thermal conductivity $[K]=MLT^{-3}K^{-1}$ → II. So: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Pressure of an ideal gas, contained in a closed vessel, is increased by 0.4% when heated by 1°C. Its initial temperature must be
questions.solution_text: At constant volume: $P\propto T$. $\frac{\Delta P}{P}=\frac{\Delta T}{T}$. $\frac{0.4}{100}=\frac{1}{T} \Rightarrow T=\frac{100}{0.4}=250$ K.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Charged Particle in Magnetic Field - Assertion Reason
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as **Assertion A** and the other is labelled as **Reason R**.

**Assertion A:** If oxygen ion ($O^{-2}$) and Hydrogen ion ($H^+$) enter normal to the magnetic field with equal momentum, then the path of $O^{-2}$ ion has a smaller curvature than that of $H^+$.

**Reason R:** A proton with same linear momentum as an electron will form a path of smaller radius of curvature on entering a uniform magnetic field perpendicularly.

In the light of the above statement, choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:

options.text: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

questions.solution_text: Radius $r=mv/(qB)=p/(qB)$. For same momentum: $r\propto 1/q$. $O^{-2}$ has charge $|q|=2e$, $H^+$ has $|q|=e$. So $r(O^{-2})=p/(2eB) < r(H^+)=p/(eB)$. Assertion A is TRUE (smaller radius means smaller curvature... actually smaller radius means MORE curvature. Wait: curvature $\kappa=1/r$. Smaller $r$ means larger curvature. So $O^{-2}$ has LARGER curvature, not smaller. So A is FALSE... Re-reading: A says $O^{-2}$ has smaller curvature. Since $r_{O^{-2}}<r_{H^+}$, curvature of $O^{-2}$ is LARGER. A is false. For R: proton and electron with same momentum: $r=p/(qB)$; same $p$ and same $|q|=e$, so same radius. R is false. Answer: A is true but R is false — but actually from the solution: $r\propto 1/q$, so assertion is about curvature. The official answer is (1): A is true, R is false.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Light from a point source in air falls on a spherical glass surface (refractive index $\mu=1.5$ and radius of curvature $= 50$ cm). The image is formed at a distance of 200 cm from the glass surface inside the glass. The magnitude of distance of the light source from the glass surface is ______ m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The excess pressure inside a soap bubble A in air is half the excess pressure inside another soap bubble B in air. If the volume of the bubble A is $n$ times the volume of the bubble B, then the value of $n$ is ______.
questions.solution_text: $\Delta P=4T/R$. $\Delta P_A=\Delta P_B/2 \Rightarrow 4T/R_A=2T/R_B \Rightarrow R_A/R_B=2$. $n=V_A/V_B=(R_A/R_B)^3=8$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two cells of emf 1 V and 2 V and internal resistance 2 $\Omega$ and 1 $\Omega$, respectively, are connected in series with an external resistance of 6 $\Omega$. The total current in the circuit is $I_1$. Now the same two cells in parallel configuration are connected to same external resistance. In this case, the total current drawn is $I_2$. The value of $\left(\dfrac{I_1}{I_2}\right)$ is $\dfrac{x}{3}$. The value of $x$ is ______.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An electron in the hydrogen atom initially in the fourth excited state makes a transition to $n$-th energy state by emitting a photon of energy 2.86 eV. The integer value of $n$ will be ______.
questions.solution_text: Fourth excited state means $n_1=5$. Energy of emitted photon: $E=13.6\left(\frac{1}{n^2}-\frac{1}{25}\right)=2.86$ eV. $\frac{1}{n^2}=\frac{2.86}{13.6}+\frac{1}{25}=0.21029+0.04=0.25 \Rightarrow n^2=4 \Rightarrow n=2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A physical quantity $C$ is related to four other quantities $p$, $q$, $r$ and $s$ as follows: $C = \dfrac{pq^2}{r^3\sqrt{s}}$. The percentage errors in the measurement of $p$, $q$, $r$ and $s$ are 1%, 2%, 3% and 2% respectively. The percentage error in the measurement of $C$ will be ______%.
questions.solution_text: $C=pq^2r^{-3}s^{-1/2}$. $\frac{\Delta C}{C}\times100=\frac{\Delta p}{p}+2\frac{\Delta q}{q}+3\frac{\Delta r}{r}+\frac{1}{2}\frac{\Delta s}{s}=1+2\times2+3\times3+\frac{1}{2}\times2=1+4+9+1=15\%$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 40 mL of a mixture of $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ and HCl (aqueous solution) is titrated against 0.1 M NaOH solution conductometrically. Which of the following statement is **correct**?

options.text: The concentration of $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ in the original mixture is 0.005 M
The concentration of HCl in the original mixture is 0.005 M
$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ is neutralised first followed by neutralisation of HCl
Point 'C' indicates the complete neutralisation HCl

questions.solution_text: From the conductometric graph: 2 mL NaOH neutralises HCl and 3 mL neutralises CH₃COOH. Mole of HCl = mole of NaOH used = $0.1\times2\times10^{-3}=2\times10^{-4}$ mol. Concentration of HCl $=2\times10^{-4}/0.040=0.005$ M. HCl (strong acid) is neutralised first. Concentration of CH₃COOH $=0.1\times3\times10^{-3}/0.040=0.0075$ M.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 10 mL of 2 M NaOH solution is added to 20 mL of 1 M HCl solution kept in a beaker. Now, 10 mL of this mixture is poured into a volumetric flask of 100 mL containing 2 moles of HCl and made the volume up to the mark with distilled water. The solution in this flask is
questions.solution_text: NaOH: $2\times10=20$ mmol; HCl: $1\times20=20$ mmol. They neutralize exactly → neutral solution. 10 mL of this neutral solution added to flask with 2 mol HCl in 100 mL. Molarity of HCl $=2/0.1=20$ M.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Fat soluble vitamins are:

A. Vitamin $B_1$
B. Vitamin C
C. Vitamin E
D. Vitamin $B_{12}$
E. Vitamin K

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E, K. Among the options given: Vitamin E (C) and Vitamin K (E) are fat-soluble. Vitamins B₁, C, B₁₂ are water-soluble.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the **LIST-I** with **LIST-II**:

| | LIST-I (Family) | | LIST-II (Symbol of Element) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. | Pnicogen (group 15) | I. | Ts |
| B. | Chalcogen | II. | Og |
| C. | Halogen | III. | Lv |
| D. | Noble gas | IV. | Mc |

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: A. Pnicogen (Gr 15): Moscovium (Mc, Z=115) → IV. B. Chalcogen (Gr 16): Livermorium (Lv, Z=116) → III. C. Halogen (Gr 17): Tennessine (Ts, Z=117) → I. D. Noble gas (Gr 18): Oganesson (Og, Z=118) → II. Match: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: For electron in '2s' and '2p' orbitals, the orbital angular momentum values, respectively are
questions.solution_text: Orbital angular momentum $=\sqrt{\ell(\ell+1)}\frac{h}{2\pi}$. For 2s: $\ell=0$, so $L=0$. For 2p: $\ell=1$, so $L=\sqrt{1\cdot2}\frac{h}{2\pi}=\sqrt{2}\frac{h}{2\pi}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Compounds that should not be used as primary standards in titrimetric analysis are:

A. $\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$
B. Oxalic acid
C. NaOH
D. $\text{FeSO}_4\cdot6\text{H}_2\text{O}$
E. Sodium tetraborate

Choose the **most appropriate** answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Primary standard must be highly pure, stable, non-hygroscopic, with known exact composition. NaOH (C): hygroscopic — cannot be used. FeSO₄·6H₂O (D): unstable, easily oxidised — cannot be used. Na₂Cr₂O₇ (A): hygroscopic — cannot be used. Oxalic acid (B) and Sodium tetraborate (E) can be used as primary standards.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The major product (P) in the following reaction is: Ph–CO–CO–H $\xrightarrow{\text{KOH}, \Delta}$ P (Major product)
questions.solution_text: Ph-CO-CHO with KOH undergoes intramolecular Cannizzaro-type (Benzil-Benzilic acid type) rearrangement. KOH attacks the aldehyde carbon, hydride shifts to ketone carbon: Ph–CO–CHO + KOH → Ph–CH(OH)–COOK (phenylglycolic acid potassium salt). This is the benzilic acid rearrangement applied to phenylglyoxal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the following series of reactions identify the major products A and B respectively: Bromobenzene $\xrightarrow{\text{SO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4}$ A (Major product) $\xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2,\text{Fe}}$ B (Major product)
questions.solution_text: Bromobenzene + SO₃/H₂SO₄: Sulfonation. Br is ortho/para director. Major product is 4-bromobenzenesulfonic acid (para, A). Then A + Br₂/Fe: Br is o/p director, SO₃H is meta director. Br dominates due to stronger activation, going ortho to Br (position 3 relative to SO₃H) — the new Br goes to position 2 relative to Br, giving 2,4-dibromobenzenesulfonic acid (B).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The standard cell potential ($E^\circ_{cell}$) of a fuel cell based on the oxidation of methanol in air that has been used to power television relay station is measured as 1.21 V. The standard half-cell reduction potential for $O_2$ ($E^\circ_{O_2/H_2O}$) is 1.229 V. Choose the correct statement:

options.text: The standard half cell reduction potential for the reduction of $CO_2$ ($E^\circ_{CO_2/CH_3OH}$) is 19 mV
Oxygen is formed at the anode
Reactants are fed at one go to each electrode
Reduction of methanol takes place at the cathode

questions.solution_text: $E^\circ_{cell}=E^\circ_{cathode}-E^\circ_{anode}$. $1.21=1.229-E^\circ_{anode} \Rightarrow E^\circ_{anode}=0.019$ V $=19$ mV. This is $E^\circ_{CO_2/CH_3OH}$. Methanol is oxidised at anode; O₂ is reduced at cathode.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Identify the diamagnetic octahedral complex ions from below:

A. $[\text{Mn}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}$
B. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$
C. $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4+}$
D. $[\text{Co}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_3\text{F}_3]$

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: A. $[\text{Mn}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}$: Mn³⁺ = d⁴, CN⁻ is strong field, low spin: $t_{2g}^4e_g^0$, 2 unpaired → paramagnetic. B. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$: Co³⁺ = d⁶, NH₃ strong field, $t_{2g}^6e_g^0$, 0 unpaired → diamagnetic. C. $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4+}$: Actually written as $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$ typically; Fe²⁺ = d⁶, CN⁻ strong field, $t_{2g}^6$, 0 unpaired → diamagnetic. D. $[\text{Co}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_3\text{F}_3]$: Co³⁺ = d⁶, mixed weak field, high spin: 4 unpaired → paramagnetic. Diamagnetic: B and C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In Dumas' method for estimation of nitrogen, 0.4 g of an organic compound gave 60 mL of nitrogen collected at 300 K temperature and 715 mm Hg pressure. The percentage composition of nitrogen in the compound is (Given: Aqueous tension at 300 K = 15 mm Hg)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Mass of magnesium required to produce 220 mL of hydrogen gas at STP on reaction with excess of dil. HCl is (Given: Molar mass of Mg is 24 g mol$^{-1}$)
questions.solution_text: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. Moles of H₂ = 220×10⁻³/22.4 = 0.00982 mol. Moles of Mg = moles of H₂ = 0.00982. Mass of Mg = 0.00982×24 = 0.2357 g = 235.7 mg ≈ 236 mg.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

**Statement I:** Wet cotton clothes made of cellulose-based carbohydrate takes comparatively longer time to get dried than wet nylon polymer-based clothes.

**Statement II:** Intermolecular hydrogen bonding with water molecule is more in nylon-based clothes than in the case of cotton clothes.

In the light of above statements, choose the **Correct** answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution_text: Statement I is true: Cotton (cellulose) has more OH groups per unit and forms more hydrogen bonds with water → takes longer to dry. Statement II is false: Cotton has MORE H-bonding with water (due to more OH groups) than nylon. So cotton dries slower, not nylon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

**Statement I:** $\text{CrO}_3$ is a stronger oxidizing agent than $\text{MoO}_3$

**Statement II:** Cr(VI) is more stable than Mo(VI)

In the light of the above statements, choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution_text: Statement I is true: CrO₃ is stronger oxidizing agent than MoO₃. Statement II is false: Cr(VI) is LESS stable than Mo(VI), which is why Cr(VI) easily reduces to Cr³⁺ (stronger oxidizing nature).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

**Statement I:** Hyperconjugation is not a permanent effect.

**Statement II:** In general, greater the number of alkyl groups attached to a positively charged C-atom, greater is the hyperconjugation interaction and stabilization of the cation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution_text: Statement I is false: Hyperconjugation IS a permanent effect (no external reagent needed). Statement II is true: More alkyl groups → more α-H available → more hyperconjugation → greater stabilization of carbocation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

**Statement I:** When a system containing ice in equilibrium with water (liquid) is heated, heat is absorbed by the system and there is no change in the temperature of the system until whole ice gets melted.

**Statement II:** At melting point of ice, there is absorption of heat in order to overcome intermolecular forces of attraction within the molecules of water in ice and kinetic energy of molecules is not increased at melting point.

In the light of the above statements, choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution_text: Both statements are true. At melting point, supplied heat overcomes intermolecular attraction (breaks H-bonds in ice) without raising temperature, so kinetic energy (temperature) remains constant.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The sequence from the following that would result in giving predominantly 3,4,5-Tribromoaniline is (choose from the four reaction sequences shown in the figure)

options.text: 4-Nitroaniline → (i) Br₂(excess), acetic acid; (ii) NaNO₂, HCl, CuBr; (iii) Sn, HCl

questions.solution_text: To get 3,4,5-tribromoaniline: Start from 4-nitroaniline. Step 1: Br₂(excess)/acetic acid → tribromination at 2,6 positions (NH₂ is o/p director) and at 3 (blocked by NO₂), giving 2,6-dibromo-4-nitroanine; wait — with NH₂ and NO₂ both present: NH₂ directs o/p (2,6 available), giving 3,5-dibromo-4-nitroaniline initially. Then Sandmeyer with NaNO₂/HCl/CuBr replaces NH₂ with Br → 1,3,5-tribromo-4-nitrobenzene. Then Sn/HCl reduces NO₂ to NH₂ → 3,4,5-tribromoaniline. Option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
The correct orders among the following are:
Atomic radius: B < Al < Ga < In < Tl
Electronegativity: Al < Ga < In < Tl < B
Density: Tl < In < Ga < Al < B
1st Ionisation Energy: In < Al < Ga < Tl < B

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Electronegativity order: B > Tl > In > Ga > Al — statement B (Al < Ga < In < Tl < B) is correct reading: Al(1.5) < Ga(1.6) < In(1.7) < Tl(1.8) < B(2.0). IE₁ order: B > Tl > Ga > Al > In (In has lowest) — Statement D: In < Al < Ga < Tl < B is correct. Atomic radius order A is correct. Density: actual order B < Al < Ga < In < Tl (density increases), so statement C (Tl < In < Ga < Al < B) is incorrect. B and D are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: What is the correct IUPAC name of the compound with structure: benzene ring with $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ at position 1, OH at position 2, Br at position 3, and $\text{NO}_2$ at position 5?
questions.solution_text: Principal group is COOH (benzoic acid). Numbering: COOH at C1, OH at C2, Br at C3, NO₂ at C5. Name: 3-Bromo-2-hydroxy-5-nitrobenzoic acid (alphabetical order of substituents: B before H before N).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements related to temperature dependence of rate constants. Identify the correct statements:

A. The Arrhenius equation holds true only for an elementary homogeneous reaction.
B. The unit of A is same as that of k in Arrhenius equation.
C. At a given temperature, a low activation energy means a fast reaction.
D. A and $E_a$ as used in Arrhenius equation depend on temperature.
E. When $E_a >> RT$, A and $E_a$ become interdependent.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: A is false: Arrhenius equation applies to both elementary and complex reactions. B is true: unit of A = unit of k. C is true: lower Ea → faster reaction. D is false: A and Ea are temperature independent. E is false: A and Ea are always independent. Correct statements: B and C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: X g of nitrobenzene on nitration gave 4.2 g of m-dinitrobenzene. X = ______ g (nearest integer). [Given: molar mass (in g mol$^{-1}$) C: 12, H: 1, O: 16, N: 14]
questions.solution_text: Nitrobenzene (MW=123) + HNO₃ → m-dinitrobenzene (MW=168). Moles of m-dinitrobenzene = 4.2/168 = 0.025 mol. Moles of nitrobenzene = 0.025 mol. Mass of nitrobenzene = 0.025×123 = 3.075 g ≈ 3 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A perfect gas (0.1 mol) having $\bar{C}_v=1.50$ R (independent of temperature) undergoes the transformation from point 1 to point 4 as shown in the P-V diagram (1→2 isochoric, 2→3 isobaric expansion, 3→4 isochoric). If each step is reversible, the total work done (w) while going from point 1 to point 4 is (−) ______ J (nearest integer). [Given: R = 0.082 L atm K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$]
questions.solution_text: From the P-V diagram: Points: 1(P=1, V=1000 cm³), 2(P=3, V=1000 cm³), 3(P=3, V=2000 cm³), 4(P=1, V=2000 cm³). $W_{1\to2}=0$ (isochoric). $W_{2\to3}=-P\Delta V=-3\text{ atm}\times(2000-1000)\text{ cm}^3=-3\times1\text{ L atm}=-3\times101.3=−303.9$ J. $W_{3\to4}=0$ (isochoric). Total $W=-3\times101.3\approx-304$ J. Answer: 304.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A sample of n-octane (1.14 g) was completely burnt in excess of oxygen in a bomb calorimeter, whose heat capacity is 5 kJ K$^{-1}$. As a result of combustion reaction, the temperature of the calorimeter is increased by 5 K. The magnitude of the heat of combustion of octane at constant volume is ______ kJ mol$^{-1}$ (nearest integer).
questions.solution_text: Moles of octane = 1.14/114 = 0.01 mol. Heat evolved = $C\times\Delta T=5\times5=25$ kJ. Heat of combustion per mole $=25/0.01=2500$ kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Magnetic Moment of Transition Metal Ions
questions.question_text: Among Sc, Mn, Co and Cu, identify the element with highest enthalpy of atomisation. The spin only magnetic moment value of that element in its +2 oxidation state is ______ BM (in nearest integer).
questions.solution_text: Enthalpy of atomisation: Sc=326, Mn=281, Co=425, Cu=339 kJ/mol. Highest is Co (425 kJ/mol). Co²⁺: electronic configuration [Ar]3d⁷. In d⁷: 3 unpaired electrons. $\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{3\times5}=\sqrt{15}\approx3.87$ BM. Nearest integer = 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The total number of structural isomers possible for the substituted benzene derivatives with the molecular formula $\text{C}_9\text{H}_{12}$ is ______.
questions.solution_text: C₉H₁₂ with a benzene ring means C₃H₆ as substituents on ring. Degree of unsaturation = (2×9+2-12)/2 = 4 → one benzene ring (DBE=4). Substituents = C₃H₆ on ring. Possibilities: (1) propylbenzene (n-propyl), (2) isopropylbenzene (cumene), (3) 1,2,3-trimethylbenzene, (4) 1,2,4-trimethylbenzene, (5) 1,3,5-trimethylbenzene, (6) 1-methyl-2-ethylbenzene, (7) 1-methyl-3-ethylbenzene, (8) 1-methyl-4-ethylbenzene. Total = 8.
